messages:
incident-bot: Paging: P1 runtime-regression detected for rollout 'ramp-wave-7' — elevated p95 latency and partial 503s. Alerting oncall.

alice (oncall): I'm on it. seeing p95 jump from 120ms -> 1.1s in us-east-1 for model variant v2.

ben (runtime): early telemetry shows kernel-fallbacks on some hosts after the new batching heuristics. hit rate ~12% of requests, correlated with sequence length >2048.

carol (sre): load patterns? any sudden traffic spikes? dashboards show modest traffic change but increased tail.

alice (oncall): no traffic surge, QPS steady. Rolling canary traffic from 5% -> 25% over 10m when metric diverged.

ben (runtime): reproducible locally with a sample replay: 
```
RPC: /generate
model: redwood-v2-quant
flags: prefetch_v2=true, batch_window_ms=12
input_len: 2600
observed: kernel fallback, long kernel compile paths, KV cache thrash
```

dave (pm): Customer impact? any errors surfaced to users or SLOs breached?

emily (support): We have two enterprise customers reporting latency spikes; support ticket numbers #CS-1209, #CS-1210. Both saw timeouts ~30s.

carol (sre): impact footprint: ~10% of requests in canary saw p99>15s, 1.7% 503s. Not global. Region: us-east primarily.

alice (oncall): Mitigation plan: 1) pause rollout (stop traffic increase), 2) flip feature flag prefetch_v2 -> false for canary hosts, 3) if persists, roll back to previous model variant. Opinions? :thumbsup: :thumbsdown:

ben (runtime): flipping prefetch_v2 off is low-risk, will remove the new prefetch path and restore older batching. I'll prep the flag flip: `./ffctl set prefetch_v2 false --selector canary=ramp-wave-7`

carol (sre): I'll hold traffic at current weight and prep capacity increase as contingency (add 10% pool).

alice (oncall): Done step 1 (paused traffic ramp). Executing flag flip now.

ben (runtime): Flag flipped. Observability: p95 dropping to ~180ms within 90s on canary hosts. No more kernel fallback traces in logs.

incident-bot: Update: alarm state cleared for group ramp-wave-7 in us-east-1 at 1745605420.

dave (pm): Good catch. We should block ramp-wave-7 until we get a postmortem and tighter preflight on sequence-length distributions.

emily (support): Notified customers with ETA to follow. They've paused impacted workflows for now.

carol (sre): Next steps: collect artifact bundle from canary hosts, include perf traces and kernel selection logs. Ben, please attach your local repro + replay.

ben (runtime): will upload replay + perf traces to the incident folder: gs://redwood-incidents/rampwave-1745604321/replay.tar.gz

alice (oncall): Handoff in 30m to second oncall. Leaving notes in pager. If anyone needs me re-alert.

incident-bot: Handoff scheduled: alice (oncall) -> carol (sre) at 1745606120.

carol (sre): Acknowledged. I'll continue until postmortem complete. Thanks everyone. :heart:
